definitions.gloss: value; numerical value; reading (of a measurement)
definitions.explanation: A number or quantity obtained from a calculation, measurement, or data. Very common in technical, scientific, and computing contexts.
The quality of being worthwhile or having merit. Often used in the pattern ～に{値|あたい}する (to be worth ~).

examples.japanese: xの{値|あたい}を{求|もと}めなさい。
{血圧|けつあつ}の{値|あたい}が{高|たか}い。
examples.english: My blood pressure reading is high.

examples.japanese: この{関数|かんすう}は{入力|にゅうりょく}された{値|あたい}に{応|おう}じて{異|こと}なる{結果|けっか}を{返|かえ}す。
examples.english: This function returns different results depending on the input value.

examples.japanese: {読|よ}む{値|あたい}のある{本|ほん}だ。
{信頼|しんらい}に{値|あたい}する{人物|じんぶつ}だ。
examples.english: He's a person worthy of trust.

examples.japanese: この{発見|はっけん}はノーベル{賞|しょう}に{値|あたい}すると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: This discovery is said to be worthy of a Nobel Prize.

notes:
The kanji {値|あたい} has two main readings: あたい (this entry) and ね (see entry 03527). The reading あたい is used for abstract/technical values and the "worth" meaning, while ね is used for prices of goods ({値段|ねだん}, {値上|ねあ}げ).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {値|あたい}を{求|もと}める: to find/calculate a value
- ～に{値|あたい}する: to be worth ~, to deserve ~
- {数値|すうち}: numerical value
- {初期|しょき}{値|あたい}: initial value (computing)
- {閾値|しきいち}/{閾値|いきち}: threshold value

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {値|ね}: price (everyday word for the cost of goods)
- {価値|かち}: value, worth (more abstract)
- {数値|すうち}: numerical value (synonym in technical contexts)
